text:
tara: quick follow-up from today's RFC — still worried about mixed-batch MQA->GQA fallback path. hit a small perf regression in staging this morning, want to sync on mitigation and rollout plan. TL;DR: grouped-query is faster for long queries but falls back too eagerly for mixed seq batches.

daniel: can you paste the staging perf snapshot?

tara: pasted below. this was a 1000q run with 30% short seq (<64) and 70% long (>512). median p95 token-latency increased by ~18% after the kernel selector change.

```
model: r-infer-3b-q8
kernel_selector: dynamic
selection_stats: { grouped_query: 64%, multi_query: 36% }
latency: { p50: 42ms, p95: 210ms -> 248ms }
kv_cache_hit: 0.74
```

sophia: That matches the hypothesis: selector heuristics are using seq_len_ratio alone and ignoring cache hit / kv profile. grouped-query has higher per-token cost when kv miss is high.

ashok: agreed. two things: make selector multi-signal (seq_len_ratio + kv_hit_rate + quant_mode) and add a hysteresis so we don't flip kernels inside a single request.

miriam: what about the cache key format? when we switch kernels the KV cache layout differs and we get invalidations => extra recompute. need an adapter so cached prefixes remain usable across kernels.

ashok: yeah, we should add a thin shim: canonicalize cache keys and store kernel-specific metadata. selector can then consult `kv_compat` flag before switching.

ashok: quick config sketch:

```
kernel_selection:
  prefer: grouped_query
  fallback: multi_query
  signals:
    - seq_len_ratio: {threshold: 1.6, weight: 0.5}
    - kv_hit_rate: {threshold: 0.65, weight: 0.3}
    - quant_mode: {prefers: multi_query, weight: 0.2}
  flip_window_ms: 150
```

daniel: love the weighted signals. need to define what we measure for kv_hit_rate (per-shard or per-request avg?).

tara: propose per-request moving avg over last 128 tokens, plus expose seq_len_distribution in traces. keep thresholds conservative for now.

sophia: also: ensure runtime API boundary stays clean — the router should ask `kernel_capabilities` and `cache_compat` from the kernel interface rather than embedding kernel internals. prevents leakage into higher layers.

miriam: rollout plan:
- add telemetry attn_kernel.selection, tags=(kernel,seq_len_bucket,kv_hit_rate_bucket,quant_mode)
- unit tests for cache shim compatibility
- canary: 1% traffic with full eval set + perf watchdog
- ramp to 10% after 24h if no regressions

tara: sounds good. can we get a perf guard in console? alarm if p95 token-latency increases >10% vs baseline for canary?

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary job started for `kernel-selector-v2` on cluster prod-gpu-3, canary=1%.

daniel: test harness request: add a mixed-batch workload generator (short+long) to our perf-suite, with KV cache warm/cold modes. I can take this.

ashok: i'll prototype the selector weights + flip_window. sophia can you define the kernel interface `kernel_capabilities` proto?

sophia: on it. will add fields: supports_grouped_query(bool), kv_compat_profiles(list), quant_preference(enum).

tara: assign owners: daniel -> perf harness + experiments; ashok -> selector impl + unit tests; sophia -> kernel interface proto + doc; miriam -> telemetry + console alarms. I'll draft the RFC follow-up summary and link to the canary when infra-bot reports metrics.

miriam: quick note: add a gauge for `cache_adapter.misses_due_to_kernel_switch` so we can detect whether shim is effective.

tara: perfect. thanks all. action items in #runtim-ops doc. please drop updates here. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary healthcheck passed (initial), metrics streaming to prometheus `attn_kernel.canary.kernel-selector-v2`.

sophia: one more edge-case — model parallel sharding: grouped_query kernels assume contiguous attention blocks; if sharding changes layout, kernel may not support compatibility. add `kernel_capabilities.shard_layouts` to proto.

ashok: noted. will add `shard_layouts` and fallback path to reject switch if incompatible.

tara: ok wrapping up. next sync in tomorrow standup unless someone hits blockers.
